title: Personal SDK Presets & Rituals — Lab Notes (draft)
content:
Purpose:
Capture a lightweight, repeatable set of personal developer presets (env, tooling, telemetry toggles) and the first-5-minutes + end-of-day rituals for engineers adopting Redwood SDKs. This is a working notebook for the devexp team to prototype UX and shipping artifacts (presets, example devcontainers, CLI flags).

Audience:
- New SDK integrators (engineers)
- DevExp engineers writing onboarding flows and quickstarts
- Solutions engineers who help customers replicate internal setups

Assumptions / constraints:
- Target machines: macOS and Linux dev laptops, plus CI runners (Ubuntu 22.04).
- Prefer minimal friction: presets that require setting 3–6 env vars, one devcontainer file, and CLI flags.
- Telemetry must be opt-out by default during internal trials (but telem opt-in flows still instrumented).

Goals (MVP):
1) Ship three named profiles: explorer, integrator, and production-sim. Each profile maps to a small env var list + recommended devcontainer snippet.
2) Create a 2-minute first-5-minutes checklist for getting a sample app to call Redwood (includes token handling and safe defaults).
3) Provide a simple toggle for local telemetry + a short script to scrub keys before sharing logs.
4) Produce a single-page quickstart that fits in our SDK README and Console onboarding flow.

Profiles (proposal):
- explorer: lowest friction, free-tier tokens, verbose examples.
  ENV: REDWOOD_API_KEY=<<free-sandbox-key>>, REDWOOD_ENV=hosted, REDWOOD_TELEM=off
  Use case: hackathons, PoCs, tutorials

- integrator: realistic usage, example batching and timeout defaults.
  ENV: REDWOOD_API_KEY=<<team-staging-key>>, REDWOOD_ENV=dedicated, REDWOOD_BATCH_SZ=8, REDWOOD_TIMEOUT_MS=3000, REDWOOD_TELEM=on
  Use case: integration tests, sample apps for customers

- production-sim: perf-oriented, kv-cache enabled, quantization hinting.
  ENV: REDWOOD_API_KEY=<<reserved-key>>, REDWOOD_ENV=private, REDWOOD_CACHE=on, REDWOOD_QUANT_HINT=4bit, REDWOOD_TELEM=on
  Use case: load tests, latency benching, SLO investigations

Devcontainer snippet (example to include in repo):
```
// .devcontainer/devcontainer.json (excerpt)
{
  "name": "redwood-sdk-explorer",
  "image": "mcr.microsoft.com/vscode/devcontainers/base:ubuntu"
  // NOTE: full file will be included in quickstart repo
}
```
(We will include a small shell init script that prompts for which profile to enable and writes an .env.local file.)

First-5-minutes checklist (two-minute flow):
1) Clone sample repo (link in quickstart).
2) cp .env.example .env.local and paste sandbox key.
3) npm install / poetry install.
4) yarn dev or python app.py (one command).
5) Run smoke: curl -s -X POST http://localhost:3000/api/generate -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'
If it responds, success. If 401, ensure REDWOOD_API_KEY is set and not expired.

End-of-day / share-safe ritual:
- run scripts/scrub-keys.sh to remove tokens from local logs and .env.local before pushing.
- telemetry: run scripts/telem-toggle.sh off if you want to stop reporting dev telemetry.

Telemetry policy (short):
- Default for internal builds: REDWOOD_TELEM=on to help product tuning.
- Defaults for public quickstarts and workshops: REDWOOD_TELEM=off.
- All telemetry events are documented in the Console telemetry catalog (link in linked_artifacts).

Open UX questions (to resolve in sprint):
- Should profiles be implemented as named subcommands in the redwood CLI (e.g., redwood profile apply explorer) or as a small npm package we add to sample repos?
- How granular should the preset overrides be? Per-route overrides may be useful but add complexity.
- Can we generate a lightweight profile badge that users can copy into README to indicate which profile was used to test?

Implementation plan (sketch):
- Week 1: finalize env var schema and create three canonical .env.example files (one per profile). Link a PR template that references the profile used for tests. (Owner: Marco)
- Week 2: author devcontainer and scrubbing scripts, add telemetry toggle script. (Owner: Priya)
- Week 3: integrate profile apply command into CLI (POC), add to quickstart README, and run internal pilot. (Owner: Jonah)

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- New user can follow the 2-minute flow and get a sample app calling Redwood within 5 minutes on macOS/Ubuntu.
- scrub-keys.sh removes all recognized token patterns from repo and logs.
- QA bench: production-sim runs a 1000-request latency sweep in CI and produces a short report.

Notes to self / fragments:
- Consider a tiny web UI in the Console that generates profile snippets for users (copy button).
- For training sessions: one slide that shows the three profiles and recommended usage.
- Reminder: gate any default production hints behind an explicit 'production-sim' flag to avoid accidental misuse.

References / links:
- Confluence spec (working): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/SDK+profiles+proposal
- Draft PR for profile env loader: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/412
- Jira card for CLI profile command: JIRA-RDW-2345

TODO (short):
- [ ] Write scrub-keys.sh with token regex (Aisha)
- [ ] Draft devcontainer example and test on Ubuntu (Priya)
- [ ] Add 'profile apply' to CLI POC and gather feedback (Jonah)
- [ ] Create single-page quickstart for README and Console (Marco)

Unresolved risks:
- Too many profiles will confuse users; keep to 3 maximum for MVP.
- Telemetry defaults need legal review for public quickstarts (flagged for compliance).

If you iterate on this doc, please prefix updated versions with a date and short changelog at the top.

-- end of lab notes --
